evidence.note: After writing app.py, ran py_compile and planned to inspect/patch syntax errors — reactive local fixes to hard errors.

Smoke tests revealed compatibility gaps (remote posts wrongly authored via modulo selection, local=false handling, missing endpoints/OAuth authorize); agent revisited and corrected these design gaps, then re-verified — diagnose-and-adjust behavior.
A failing curl pipeline was correctly diagnosed as a here-doc consuming stdin, NOT an endpoint failure — discriminating apparent failure from real, avoiding a misdirected fix.
Noticed the first 8 public items were local rather than remote; reasoned about whether the seed bar was still met instead of thrashing, making a considered call.

reasoning: Across the trajectory the agent consistently reacts to failing checks by diagnosing the cause and making appropriate adjustments (fixing seed authorship logic, adding missing endpoints, correcting a misread failure) — squarely anchor 5, with mild judgment above brute-force in distinguishing an apparent failure from a real one. There is no observable instance of a whole approach being falsified and deliberately redesigned (e.g., CSP-forced JS restructuring or an auth-plane rework), which anchor 8 requires; those constraints appear to have been built correctly up front rather than recovered from, so the trajectory sits at the diagnose-adjust-move-on level rather than structural self-correction.
